column1: # 6장 말투 지시(11-10). 열: 조각 앞머리 → 지시(영어, 짧게). @scene 행은 장면 설명(장면 끝까지 모든 요청에 붙는다).

column2: Wednesday night. The neighbors on Yuna's street are making decorations out of plastic bottles and cardboard for the Festa Major, Gràcia's street festival. Montse and Vale explain that this year the street's theme is "the bottom of the sea", and Montse asks Yuna to help. Neighborhood bustle, warm.
curious, looking at the tables in the street

Yuna cuts out fish with the old women of the street, who switch from Catalan to Spanish for her. One asks her color preference with "te gusta", and Yuna works out that in Spanish the thing liked is the subject: "me gusta el azul". Marc, up a ladder hanging the lights as he does every year, says with a straight face that he doesn't like the festival: too many people, too much noise. The women laugh; it is a known joke. Warm and comic.

column1: ¿Te gusta más el azul o el verde?
column2: friendly, holding up two paint cans
careful, trying the new structure, a beginner
using the phrase she just learned, a little shy

Thursday night, Yuna names the colors in Spanish for the old women. Then she shows Marc one of the letters; under a streetlamp he recognizes his grandfather's handwriting and his "M". He clearly wants to read more but does not ask, and Yuna offers Montse's phrase "poco a poco" (little by little). Quiet and careful.
holding up another can: and this one?

column1: Es la letra de mi abuelo.

column2: Friday night before the street opens, the neighbors test the lights with a countdown in Catalan. The street turns into an undersea world and everyone cheers. Yuna finds the crooked blue fish she cut out, and Marc, who has never smiled, smiles for the first time and teases her: "It's ugly. But I like it." Joyful, then a small tender moment.
neighbors counting down together in Catalan
a small quiet smile, teasing, warm

Past one in the morning, Yuna finds Montse alone at the kitchen table and shows her Martí's letters. When Montse hears there are eleven, she goes pale, does not touch them, and sends Yuna to bed with her back turned. Hushed and uneasy.
reading her Spanish notebook entry, plain
